Create a perk, the access your app checks for, and optionally the products that grant it. Asks for
what is missing in a terminal.

Usage:
  voidhash perk create [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help               Show help for this command
      --json               Print the API objects as JSON, for scripts
      --name <name>        What people see, such as Premium
      --product <product>  A product that grants it: its slug, name or id; repeat for each (can be
                           repeated)
      --project <project>  Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name (default: this
                           directory's project, then your default project)
  -q, --quiet              Print only ids, one per line
      --slug <slug>        How your code checks for it, such as premium (default: made from the
                           name)

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash perk create --name Premium
  voidhash perk create --name "Offline mode" --product pro-annual --product lifetime
